dedupe_keys.name: hurricane rita 2005 the houston and texas coast evacuation and the planning changes after it

description: This case study reviews the mass evacuation of the Houston area and Texas coast ahead of Hurricane Rita in September 2005 and the planning changes that followed. It was written by the House Research Organization of the Texas House of Representatives and published in February 2006 as an interim report, free to download online as a PDF. It draws on the state Office of Homeland Security's 2005 hurricane preparedness report and the hearings of the governor's Task Force on Evacuation, Transportation and Logistics. An estimated 3.7 million people left the Houston area and the coast between Corpus Christi and Beaumont; preliminary state figures linked 118 deaths to Rita, news reports tied at least 60 of them to the evacuation, including 23 assisted-living residents who died in a bus fire, and evacuees faced drives of 20 hours or more, fuel shortages and late contraflow on the interstates. Coverage is the Texas coast. Caveats: the report is a short policy review written before the task force's final findings, and figures were preliminary. It covers planning and coordination, traffic and contraflow, fuel supply, special-needs evacuation and public communication, and lists the recommendations under discussion. Simulation uses: an observed stress case for evacuation traffic, fuel logistics and special-needs transport models. Related records: the Florida regional evacuation study surge zones (data-florida-statewide-regional-evacuation-study-surge-zones) support comparable planning.
